stories.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors
stories.simple_summary: A tech website is guessing who might become the next boss of Nvidia if the current CEO has to leave. The company doesn't have an official plan for who would take over.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who own Nvidia stock. It doesn't affect what you buy or use.

stories.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
stories.simple_summary: The founder of Nvidia is in trouble over personal matters that involve someone from China. This is causing concern among U.S. government officials who worry about secrets being shared.
stories.why_it_matters: If Nvidia's leadership becomes unstable, it could affect the technology companies depend on, but any major changes will take time.

stories.title: Google Brings Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay
stories.simple_summary: Google's AI assistant Gemini can now work in Apple car dashboards so you can talk to it while driving. You would use voice commands like asking questions or getting help with tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: If you drive an Apple CarPlay car and like using voice assistants, this gives you another option to try.

stories.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia's board of directors may vote to fire the company's longtime CEO within days. The stock price has fallen because investors are worried about this change.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly affects Nvidia investors and stock owners. It could eventually influence the price of AI technology services, but not immediately.

stories.title: Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec
stories.simple_summary: The Nvidia CEO is accused of having a second affair, this time with someone who works at his company. This comes after he already admitted to a separate affair involving someone with connections to China.
stories.why_it_matters: This is personal scandal news. It doesn't directly change anything about AI products or services you use.

stories.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove the CEO from his job following reports of multiple affairs. One involved someone alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: Major leadership changes at a big tech company can create uncertainty, but regular people won't notice effects right away.

stories.title: Jensen Huang affair in D.C.: Resignation calls and moves to tighten Nvidia China exports
stories.simple_summary: Politicians in Washington are calling for the Nvidia CEO to resign and discussing ways to limit what technology Nvidia can sell to China. The CEO's personal behavior is now becoming a national security issue.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political and security news. For now it doesn't change what technology you can buy or use.

stories.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
stories.simple_summary: United Airlines says it won't allow AI assistants to book flights for you on its website. The airline is worried about privacy and following the law, and it hasn't seen many people try to do this anyway.
stories.why_it_matters: If you were hoping an AI assistant could automatically book your flights, you'll still need to do it yourself or call the airline.

stories.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
stories.simple_summary: Big companies want to build huge computer centers to run AI, but these projects face real problems. Local communities don't want them, paperwork takes forever, and there's not enough electricity. Many of these announced projects may never actually get built.
stories.why_it_matters: If AI services start costing more because these data centers aren't built, you might notice higher prices for AI tools. For now it's mostly just industry gossip.

stories.title: Meta is losing its longtime head of  infrastructure
stories.simple_summary: A top engineer who built computer systems at Meta for 15 years is stepping down from his job. The company hasn't said why yet.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly industry news. It could matter if it affects how well Meta's services run, but there's no sign of problems yet.

stories.title: How backlash and red tape continue to slow data centers post-Blue Wave
stories.simple_summary: Companies trying to build enormous computer centers for AI are running into obstacles. Local people don't want them in their towns, getting permits takes a long time, and power supplies are hard to find. Many planned projects may never happen.
stories.why_it_matters: If fewer of these giant computer centers get built, AI services might become more expensive for small businesses and individuals.

stories.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
stories.simple_summary: A company called CoreWeave that rents out computer power for AI projects is asking customers to pay money upfront and work with shorter contracts. This is how the company is trying to fund its growth.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to large companies renting computer power. Small businesses using AI probably won't notice a difference.
